chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who performs sajdah upon pebbles, but his forehead cannot settle upon the ground. He said: He should move his forehead until it becomes properly placed, then move the pebbles away from his forehead, and he should not raise his head.

Thus, the correct approach regarding these reports is to understand them as applying to the case in which a person is able to place his forehead evenly without raising his head, because if he raises his head, he would have added an extra sajdah in the salat, and that is not permissible. The first report is to be understood as referring to a state of necessity in which this cannot be achieved except by raising the head.

key_terms.الِاضْطِرَارِ: a state of necessity or compulsion
key_terms.الْحَصَى: small pebbles on which the forehead may fall during sajdah
key_terms.جَبْهَتَهُ: his forehead, the part required to be placed in sajdah
key_terms.سَجْدَةً: a single prostration within the salat

ai.seo_question: What should a person do in sajdah if pebbles prevent the forehead from resting properly on the ground?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling for one whose forehead lands on an elevated or unsuitable spot during sajdah. It instructs that he should adjust his forehead without lifting his head when possible, because lifting the head would amount to adding an extra sajdah in the salat; only in a state of necessity is the other report understood differently.
